name: Cappuccino RC Translation Drill
text:
1
Cappuccino RC Translation Drill
1 PASSAGE
Instructions

NOTE: Cappuccino is similar to Decaf, except instead of recapping all of your Translations after finishing with each paragraph, you’ll be looking back at the text to confirm your Translations.

Read, translate, and quip paragraph 1*. Do it just like LR.

Look away from paragraph 1 and recap the FULL TRANSLATION of paragraph 1 silently.

Take a few seconds to confirm your Translation with the paragraph you just read.

In this step, you are not rereading from scratch. 

You're confirming the Translation you already have is right. 

This style of confirming your Translation with the text applies to every confirmation you ever do on RC.

Read, translate, and quip paragraph 2. Do it just like LR.

Look away from paragraph 2 and recap the FULL TRANSLATION of paragraph 2 silently.

Take a few seconds to confirm your Translation with all the text you've read of the passage so far.

This confirmation step will include all the paragraphs you've read so far.

Repeat this pattern for all remaining paragraphs.

OPTIONAL: Look away and recap the FULL TRANSLATION of the entire passage silently.

This step is optional, but you should do it when you first begin Cappuccino RC Translation Drills and periodically afterward, just to confirm that you can.

Complete this same process on all remaining passages in the section.

SEE FULL WORKOUT DETAILS

  9. Complete this same process on all remaining passages in the section.

name: Masterpiece
text:
2
Masterpiece
Instructions

NOTE: Masterpieces are multi-day workouts focused on a single section*. You can do a three-day Masterpiece or a four-day Masterpiece to start. Don't worry, you do less and less work as the Masterpiece progresses each day.

Complete the section in any workout style.

Mark questions for hyperskip, but don't perform your hyperskip pass yet.

When you're done with the section, put it aside without grading it.

The next day, redo each question in the section fully.

When you return to the section, keep your answer selected at first, but uncross off all other answer choices.

Do not just look at your previous answer without actually redoing the full question. Your objective is to decide whether you want to stick to your previous answer or choose a new answer.

On each question you have three options:

Lock in your previous answer.

Once an answer is locked, you will not look at this question again until Camo Day. Locking is a way to signal to yourself that you know this answer is correct and do not need to look at it again.

Do not lock in more than 50% of your remaining answers on any lock-in pass until you get to the last day of your Masterpiece.

Keep your answer the same, but leave the question unlocked.

Leave a question unlocked if you are not sure about whether the answer you've selected is correct.

Change your answer.

If you change your answer, you may not lock the question on this pass.

The next day, return only to your unlocked questions and redo them. Decide to lock in or change your answers, following the same procedure you did on day 2.

This process repeats for however many days your Masterpiece will last.

Make sure all questions are locked in by the last day.

Optional: On the last day, print out a fresh copy of the section and redo it straight-through.

Compare the fresh section to your locked-in answers and see if there are any differences. If so, reconcile the two sections. Decide on your final answer before putting it into Camo.

After your last pass on the section, with all answers locked in, proceed with Camo and Wrong Answer Journaling.

SEE FULL WORKOUT DETAILS

name: Extracurricular Reading
text:
3
Extracurricular Reading
Instructions

Every day, translate elevated reading material from outside the LSAT, using the following sources:

ScienceDaily.com

Ideal daily reading for those who feel alienated by scientific language or fear science passages in RC

Be sure to choose the articles that challenge you the most, not articles that look familiar or interesting

Aeon.co

The most similar articles to LSAT RC on the internet

Reading an Aeon.co article every day is a great habit if you have no specific topic-based weaknesses, but would like to make RC-style reading a habit.

ALDaily.com

Ideal daily reading for those who feel alienated by abstract language, art, humanities, and pretension.

Be sure to choose the articles that look the most unfamiliar, not articles that speak to your pre-existing interests.

NYT Guide to Essential Knowledge

The single best way to fix gaps in common knowledge

Here is a list of sections in the Guide that are relevant to LSAT. If any of these topics would trouble you as an RC passage, read over that section of the guide.

LSAT Relevant Guide Sections: Architecture, Zoology, Botany, History, Art, Photography, Literature, Music (the serious parts about jazz and blues, especially), Film, Dance, Drama, Climate & Weather and Glossary of Weather Words (In Geography), Government, Law, Philosophy, Biology, Chemistry, Physics, Astronomy, Geology

Crash Course

Not a written source, but Crash Course is too useful for solving common knowledge gaps to not include

Watch Crash Course while you're in line, waiting for someone, on hold, brushing your teeth, etc. Any time you could be scrolling on your phone, watch Crash Course instead.

Top Five LSAT Relevant Crash Course Sections: Intellectual Property (Ellen's favorite for LSAT students), Economics, US Government & Politics, Art History, and Philosophy

SEE FULL WORKOUT DETAILS

name: Vocab Training
text:
4
Vocab Training
Instructions

Highlight any word you wouldn't bet your LSAT score on during all LSAT sections and during all Extracurricular Reading.

These highlighted words are your vocab words.

Harvest all the vocab words you've highlighted after your section or reading is complete.

Harvesting your words means writing down each of your vocab words in a tracker. You can use my template or create a simple Google Sheet for this.

Always harvest your vocab words the same day that you highlight them.

To further optimize your vocab harvesting, watch the How to Harvest Vocab Words video.

Practice your vocab words daily for at least 10 minutes.

To practice, follow the procedures outlined in the How to Learn Vocab Without AI video or the How to Learn Vocab: AI Supercharged Edition video.

10 minutes of practice is a minimum, not a maximum. If you have a 100+ number of vocab words to learn, do not be afraid to practice for a longer period of time.

SEE FULL WORKOUT DETAILS
